paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers took the bus to the port. They wanted to see the boats and write a post for the class blog. The sun was hot, and the sea was flat and blue. "This is a perfect day for photos," said Leo. Mia had her camera, Lily had her notebook, and May had a list of questions. Teacher Kim only smiled and carried her big bag.

A man from the port staff met them at the gate. He wore an orange vest. "The port is busy every day," he said. "Workers carry boxes from the boats to the trucks." "You can walk in this area," he said, "but stay behind the yellow line." Among the boats, there were red fishing boats and one big white ferry. May looked at the ferry. "When does the next ferry go?" she asked. "At eleven o'clock," said the man.

Lily looked at the sea and the sky. "Look at the birds," she said. "There were many birds on the water, but now they fly to the land." Mia took a photo of the flags above the gate. The flags moved fast now, and the wind pulled at her hair. A big cloud came over the sun, and it was not hot anymore.

The port staff looked at the sky and talked on a small radio. Leo still wanted one more photo of the ferry. "The sun is gone," he said. Then the workers pulled the fishing boats close to the wall. They tied each boat with an extra rope. "Why do you tie extra ropes?" asked Leo. "The sea is not quiet today," said the man. At the ferry, a worker changed the sign to "WAIT."

Teacher Kim opened her big bag and took out five raincoats. "I always bring them," she said. "Put on your raincoat when it rains." She gave one to Lily, one to Mia, one to Leo, one to May, and one to herself. Mia put her camera in her bag and closed it. The children walked fast to the waiting area under the roof. A cold wind came across the port, and the flags stood out flat.
Lily felt something on her hand, and then she felt it again. Lily put on her raincoat. "Now I know why the birds flew away," she said.
